0.0.n: The て-form of 妊娠する connects to から to say when the following situation began.

0.1.n: After a verb in て-form, から marks the starting point of a later situation.

0.2.n: は highlights the period after pregnancy, contrasting it with before.

0.3.n: 授業 means classes or lessons; here it refers to the speaker’s teaching duties.

0.4.n: で is part of ではなく, which rejects one option before introducing another.

0.5.n: は works with で and なく to contrast teaching classes with administrative help.

0.6.n: なく is the connecting form of ない, leaving the sentence open for the alternative.

1.0.n: 教務 combines with 事務 to describe administration related to teaching and classes.

1.1.n: 事務 refers to office tasks rather than classroom teaching.

1.2.n: の links the administrative work to the help being provided.

1.3.n: お adds a polite touch to 手伝い; here the noun describes the speaker’s supporting role.

1.4.n: として marks the role in which the speaker came to work.

1.5.n: 出勤する becomes 出勤している for an ongoing routine, then ends in て to connect to the next clause.

2.0.n: ラッシュ is borrowed from English and refers here to crowded commuting periods.

2.1.n: の links ラッシュ to 時間, identifying the period when commuting is busiest.

2.2.n: 時間 refers to a time period here, not a measured duration.

2.3.n: を marks ラッシュの時間 as what the speaker avoids.

2.4.n: The て-form of 避ける connects avoiding rush hour with coming to work.

2.5.m: was allowed to come to work
2.5.n: 出勤させてもらう presents permission as a favor received; ていた shows this arrangement continued in the past.

2.6.n: ので introduces the reason for the result in the next line.

3.0.n: 出勤 combines with 時間 to refer here to the journey to work.

3.1.n: 時間 here means the time spent commuting, not the scheduled starting time.

3.2.n: は makes the commute the topic of the statement about finding a seat.

3.3.n: 大体 describes how often she could sit, rather than an approximate quantity.

3.4.n: 座れる is the can-do form of 座る; ていました politely describes a recurring situation in the past.

0.lit: After becoming pregnant, as for that period, not classes,
0.tip: ではなく sets up a contrast: not teaching classes, but doing the administrative work mentioned next.

1.lit: As help with academic affairs administration, I was coming to work, and
1.tip: として identifies the speaker’s role: she attended work as administrative help.

2.lit: Because I had been allowed to come to work avoiding rush-hour times,
2.tip: させてもらう means receiving permission to do something, with a sense of appreciation.

3.lit: As for commuting time, I was usually able to sit.
3.tip: 座れていました expresses being able to sit regularly in the past, not simply sitting once.
